questions.question: What allocation method stores files in consecutive disk blocks?
questions.explanation: Contiguous allocation places file data in adjacent blocks. It provides fast access but suffers from external fragmentation.

questions.question: What structure maps file names to metadata and locations?
questions.explanation: Directories maintain mappings from file names to file metadata. They organize the file system namespace hierarchy.

questions.question: What tracks which disk blocks are available for allocation?
options: Both free space list and block bitmap
questions.explanation: Free space management uses either lists or bitmaps to track available blocks. Bitmaps are efficient for finding contiguous space.

questions.question: What disk scheduling algorithm serves requests in arrival order?
questions.explanation: FCFS schedules disk requests in order received. It's fair but can have poor seek time performance.

questions.question: What allocation method uses pointers to link file blocks?
questions.explanation: Linked allocation chains file blocks together using pointers. It eliminates external fragmentation but random access is slow.

questions.question: What data structure in Unix stores file metadata?
questions.explanation: Inodes store file metadata like permissions, timestamps, and block locations. The file name is stored separately in directories.

questions.question: What disk scheduling minimizes seek time by choosing nearest request?
questions.explanation: Shortest Seek Time First selects the closest pending request. It improves throughput but can cause starvation.

questions.question: What allocation method uses a block containing pointers to data blocks?
questions.explanation: Indexed allocation stores all block pointers in an index block. It supports efficient random access without fragmentation.

questions.question: What directory structure allows files to appear in multiple locations?
questions.explanation: Acyclic graph directories support links, allowing files to be referenced from multiple locations. Cycles must be prevented.

questions.question: What disk scheduling sweeps back and forth serving requests?
questions.explanation: SCAN moves the disk arm in one direction serving requests, then reverses. It's also called the elevator algorithm.

questions.question: What process attaches a file system into the directory tree?
questions.explanation: Mounting attaches a file system at a directory called the mount point. Its contents become accessible through that path.

questions.question: What filename suffix conventionally identifies a file's type?
questions.explanation: File extensions like .txt or .exe indicate file type by naming convention. The OS and applications use them to select handlers.

questions.question: What identifies a file's type using bytes stored at the start of the file?
questions.explanation: Magic numbers are signature bytes at the start of a file identifying its format. They work even when the extension is wrong.

questions.question: What Unix tool checks and repairs file system consistency?
questions.explanation: fsck scans a file system for inconsistencies like lost blocks or bad link counts. It can repair damage after crashes.

questions.question: What disk scheduling algorithm serves requests in one direction, then jumps to the beginning and repeats?
questions.explanation: C-SCAN serves requests while moving to one end, then returns to the start without serving. It gives more uniform wait times than SCAN.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of disk space allocated to a file?
questions.explanation: File systems allocate space in fixed-size blocks, also called clusters. Files occupying part of a block waste the remainder as internal fragmentation.

questions.question: What per-open-file value records the current read/write position?
questions.explanation: The file pointer tracks the current offset within an open file. Read and write operations begin at this position.

questions.question: What per-process table indexes into the system-wide open-file table?
questions.explanation: Each process keeps a file descriptor table whose entries point into the system-wide open-file table. Descriptors are small integers like 0, 1, 2.

questions.question: What link type becomes dangling when its target file is deleted?
questions.explanation: Symbolic links store a path to the target. Deleting the target leaves the symlink pointing to nothing.

questions.question: What problem leaves unusable gaps between contiguously allocated files?
questions.explanation: External fragmentation scatters free space into small holes between files. Eventually no hole is large enough for new files.

questions.question: What disk scheduling variant reverses at the last request instead of traveling to the disk end?
questions.explanation: LOOK reverses direction at the last pending request rather than the physical end of the disk. It avoids wasted arm travel.

questions.question: What dedicated region records pending file system operations for crash recovery?
questions.explanation: The journal logs metadata changes before they are applied. After a crash, committed entries are replayed to restore consistency.

questions.question: What Unix permission on a directory is required to create or delete entries in it?
questions.explanation: Write permission on a directory allows creating and removing entries. Execute permission allows traversing into it.

questions.question: What special file type in Unix represents hardware devices?
questions.explanation: Device files in /dev provide file-like access to hardware. They come in character and block varieties.

questions.question: What technique maps file contents directly into a process's virtual address space?
questions.explanation: Memory-mapped files let processes access file data through memory addresses. Page faults trigger the OS to load file blocks on demand.

questions.question: What file operation repositions the current offset without reading or writing data?
questions.explanation: Seek changes the file pointer to a specified offset. It enables random access within a file.

questions.question: A database performs frequent random reads deep inside a 2 GB file. Which allocation method performs worst?
questions.explanation: Linked allocation stores block pointers inside blocks, so random access requires traversing the chain from the start.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT stored in a Unix inode?
questions.explanation: Filenames live in directory entries that map names to inode numbers; this is what makes hard links possible.

questions.question: Process A deletes a file that process B still has open. On Unix, what does B observe?
options: It can keep using the file until it closes it
questions.explanation: unlink() removes the name, but the inode persists until the last open descriptor closes, so B keeps full access.

questions.question: Which free-space management technique uses one bit per disk block to mark free versus allocated?
questions.explanation: A bit map stores one bit per block, compact and efficient for finding contiguous free regions.

questions.question: Which in-kernel cache speeds up pathname resolution by remembering recent directory-name-to-inode lookups?
questions.explanation: The dentry cache (dcache) caches directory entries so repeated path lookups avoid re-reading directory blocks.
